title: Cursor Review (2026)
intro: Cursor is evaluated here as AI software — Cursor is an AI-native code editor (VS Code fork) with Tab completions, Agent, Cloud Agents, and MCP/skills. Hobby is free with limited Agent/Tab. Pro is $20/mo. Teams Standard is $40/user/mo (about $32 annual). Heavier Pro+/Ultra and Teams Premium SKUs exist for agent-heavy usage; Enterprise is contact sales. Paid plans include model usage allotments with overage — the seat price is not a hard cap. This review uses SoftwareGlimpse’s AI methodology (ease of use, AI job fit, output quality, workflow depth, integrations, governance/privacy, scalability, value, model capability), scoring products inside their job cluster rather than against unrelated peers. It is based on first-party research, not hands-on lab testing.
summary: Choose Cursor when the job is an AI-native coding editor and agents — not GitHub Copilot-as-a-plugin and not ChatGPT.
verdict: Choose Cursor when the job is an AI-native coding editor and agents — not GitHub Copilot-as-a-plugin and not ChatGPT. Compare GitHub Copilot if you must stay in current IDEs and GitHub policy; ChatGPT for general coding chat only. Scores reflect first-party documentation as of 2026-08-18 — not hands-on product testing. Confirm current packaging, usage caps and credit rates on the vendor site before purchase.

criterionAssessments.rationale: VS Code-familiar editor with Agent-first UX; migration cost exists but onboarding is fast for VS Code users.
AI-native coding editor — ai-code cluster peer of GitHub Copilot, not an LLM-assistant rank.
Frontier-model Agent and Tab are the quality story from vendor positioning — not a lab bake-off.
Agent, Cloud Agents, MCP, skills, and hooks are deeper than plugin-style autocomplete.
MCP and git remotes cover the coding loop; GitHub-native PR UI still belongs to Copilot/github.com.
Teams/Enterprise add SSO and privacy modes; consumer Pro is individual-grade.
Hobby → Pro → Teams → Enterprise exists; usage economics matter at agent scale.
Pro $20 matches ChatGPT Plus; Teams $40 is the procurement seat. Overage is the TCO watch-out. Affiliate economics excluded.
Explicit frontier-model Agent access is a capability lead vs autocomplete-only tools.
